Simulation of an Assembly process from a Meta-web (continuous time)

Source: R/RcppExports.R
metaWebNetAssemblyCT.Rd

This is a dynamical model of colonization and extinction process [1], similar to the TTIB model described in [2]. The interactions of the meta-web are conserved in the local web. With an additional secondary extinction rate that controls when a predator goes extinct if it has no prey.

Usage

metaWebNetAssemblyCT(metaW, m, e, se, time)

Arguments

metaW

metacommunity adyacency matrix

m

A numeric vector of species' migration rates (events per unit of time) from the meta-web

e

A numeric vector of species' extinction rates

se

A numeric vector of species' secondary extinction rates

time

Simulated time, the state is recorded at integer times 1 to time-1

Value

A list with the number of species with at least one link by time S, the number of links by time L, the time series of species presence STime (one row per species, one column per recorded time) and the adjacency matrix A with effective links.

Details

This is the continuous time version of metaWebNetAssembly(), simulated with the Gillespie algorithm [3]. There are 3 possible events: migration with rate m, local extinction with rate e, and secondary extinction, when a predator has no prey, with rate se. The parameters are vectors so each species could have their own parameter values. At each iteration only one event happens: the species and the event type are chosen with probability proportional to the rates, and the waiting time until the event is drawn from an exponential distribution with parameter equal to the sum of all rates. The state of the system is recorded at integer times 1, 2, ..., time-1.

The main differences with the discrete time version metaWebNetAssembly() are:

  • m, e and se are rates (events per unit of time) and can be larger than 1, instead of probabilities per time step in [0,1].

  • Events are asynchronous, one at a time, instead of all species being updated in each time step.

  • Secondary extinctions are not resolved in cascade within a step: a predator without prey goes extinct only when its own secondary extinction event happens, so cascades unfold over time.

  • The time series are samples of the state at integer times, and the number of events between samples is variable.

References

  1. Saravia, L. A., Marina, T. I., Kristensen, N. P., De Troch, M., & Momo, F. R. (2022). Ecological network assembly: How the regional metaweb influences local food webs. Journal of Animal Ecology, 91(3), 630–642. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2656.13652

  2. Galiana, N., Lurgi, M., Claramunt-López, B., Fortin, M.-J., Leroux, S., Cazelles, K., et al. (2018). The spatial scaling of species interaction networks. Nat. Ecol. Evol., 2, 782–790

  3. Gillespie, D. T. (1976). A general method for numerically simulating the stochastic time evolution of coupled chemical reactions. Journal of Computational Physics, 22(4), 403–434. doi: 10.1016/0021-9991(76)90041-3

See also

metaWebNetAssembly() for the discrete time version.
